title: Laplacian moment as a conditional moment
statement: Let $[?]$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $[?]$, and let a finite nonempty index set label an orthonormal basis of real functions on that set containing the constant-one function. For a positive integer $n$, a real exponent $p$, a function $f$ on $[?]^n$, and a coordinate $i$, define the conditional centered $p$th absolute moment at $x$ by averaging $|f(x_{-i},\omega)-\mathbb{E}_{\omega'}f(x_{-i},\omega')|^p$ over $[?]$, where $x_{-i}$ denotes all coordinates other than $i$. Then the product-measure mean of $|L_i f|^p$, where $L_i f$ is $f$ minus its average over coordinate $i$, equals the product-measure mean of this conditional centered moment.
